dialog.body: Finance Department, this is Janet Whitcomb. How may I help you?

Yes, hello. This is Nora Donovan. I'm calling about my property tax bill, and I'll tell you how it went, because it's been a hassle. Last Wednesday the bill came in the mail, but it came to my old place. I moved last fall, and the people there walked it over to me, which was decent of them.
I see. Ms. Donovan, are you the owner of the property, or are you renting?

I'm renting now. But the bill is for the little house I still own, and I rent the apartment where I live. So the bill went to the wrong place. Then on Friday I looked it over, and nobody ever took off anything for my age. I'm seventy-four. I figured there'd be something.
Understood. Let me address the exemption first. Newport does offer certain exemptions for seniors and for veterans. Are you asking about a senior exemption?
Senior, yes. My husband's the veteran, well, he was, but I'm not sure that counts for me. So is there a senior one, and how do I apply? Do I just write it on the bill?

No, ma'am, it isn't done on the bill. There is an application, and it has to be filed with the assessor's office. They'll tell you what documentation is required and what the eligibility conditions are. I can transfer you, or I can have a form mailed to you.

Well, mailed is the problem, isn't it? That's my other question. How do I change the mailing address? I told somebody when I moved. I think it was in October. Maybe it was November. I called, somebody said fine, and then the bill goes to the old place anyway.

The change has to be made in writing. A phone call is not sufficient for the tax records. You would submit a signed request with the property description, the old mailing address, and the new one. You can bring it to City Hall or mail it to the Finance Department.
In writing. So the call in October did nothing.
I can't see any record of that call from here, so I can't speak to it. I'm sorry for the inconvenience.
Well. Fine. Can I write the letter and put the senior thing in the same envelope, or is that two different offices?

They're handled separately. The address change goes to the tax collector's records, and the exemption application goes to the assessor. Two separate envelopes would be best, so nothing gets misrouted.

Two envelopes. All right. I'll write that down. I can't do it all right now anyway, because I have a parent-teacher conference at four, for my granddaughter, and I need to get across town before that.

Certainly. Then let me do this. I will transfer you to the assessor's office for the exemption form. If you get their voicemail, leave your name and mailing address clearly. Is there a number where you can be reached?
It's 401-555-0182. That's my cell. And the mailing address, I'll give them the new one.
Very good. I have that as 401-555-0182. Please hold while I transfer you, Ms. Donovan.
